subject: Sigma Health — technical recap & observability asks
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sigma Health — technical recap & observability asks

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few technical asks so your engineers can scope the integration: 

High-level goal
- Replace current keyword-based triage with a contextual model for routing and reranking clinical notes to the right care pathway. Expected latency target: P95 < 300ms for serving path in user-facing flows.

Integration approach we discussed
- SDK: server-side Node/Java SDK (we recommend server-side to keep keys off the browser). We'll provide example clients and a reference express + springboot snippet.
- Auth: short-lived tokens (RBAC) issued by your auth system to Redwood; optional mTLS for Dedicated/Private.
- Routing: policy-based routing (region and tier), with fallbacks to smaller quantized models for burst traffic.
- Structured output/tool calling: model will return JSON with actions (e.g., {"action":"lookup_med_history","params":{...}}) — you can map those to internal tool calls.
- Embeddings & reranker: store embeddings in your vector DB (we recommend Faiss/Elastic with encrypted volumes). A light reranker layer will be used to rescore top-K by relevance before final output.

Observability hooks (please confirm these are accessible in staging):
- Trace propagation: include incoming X-Trace-Id header; Redwood will echo an x-redwood-trace-id in responses and map to our trace for cross-service correlation.
- Logging fields: request_id, user_id (hashed), model_variant, route, batch_size, tokens_in, tokens_out, infer_latency_ms.
- Latency breakdown headers: x-queue-latency-ms, x-infer-latency-ms, x-kvcache-hit.
- Dashboards: we'll provision a per-account dashboard showing P50/P95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and per-route error rates.

Action items / asks
1) Can your infra team enable a staging endpoint with service account credentials for our spike? (we'll need basic API access + sampling of logs)
2) Confirm whether PHI will be sent to the hosted API or if you need Private deployment (on-prem / VPC).
3) Share any rate expectations (RPS) and typical request size (avg tokens in/out).

Attachments: sigma_integration_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet w/ field mapping), call_recording_20260615.mp3

Proposed immediate next step: 2-hour technical workshop + live spike next Tue (Jun 23). I've linked a Calendly slot below. Connor and Marissa will join to run the spike.

Thanks — Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@sigmahealth.com>

Cc: DevOps Team <infra@sigmahealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sigma Health — technical recap & observability asks

Rafael — thanks for the thorough summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Compliance: we handle PHI; if PHI is in requests we will require Private deployment or a BAA-backed hosted arrangement. I'll confirm with security but please assume PHI cannot go to a public multitenant endpoint for now.
- Auth: we prefer short-lived OAuth tokens issued by our identity provider (Okta). Is Redwood able to accept OAuth token exchange and map into short-lived inference tokens?
- Trace: echoing X-Trace-Id is perfect. Can you include an example trace header mapping you plan to emit so our SREs can wire into Splunk?

I'll loop in our security lead separately. The infra team can spin up a staging PRD-like cluster; we need an itemized list of what they must open (ports, certs, sample payloads).

Ok to schedule the tech workshop — Tue Jun 23 10–12 PT works for me.

Laura
Director of Engineering — Integration Platform
Sigma Health
laura.chen@sigmahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@sigmahealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-16T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sigma Health — technical recap & observability asks

Laura — quick answers while we prep the spike doc: 

- OAuth support: yes — Redwood supports token exchange (we validate short-lived OAuth tokens and mint ephemeral inference credentials). We'll include the token exchange flow diagram in the spike notes.
- PHI / Private deployment: we can run Redwood Private inside your VPC (single-tenant) or provide a dedicated tenancy with customer-managed encryption keys. We'll note options in the SOW.
- Trace header example:  
  - Incoming: X-Trace-Id: <uuid>
  - Redwood response: x-redwood-trace-id: rw-<short-id>
  - Latency headers: x-queue-latency-ms, x-infer-latency-ms, x-compile-latency-ms (if model warmup/compile occurred)

- Embeddings & rerank: recommended pipeline: client -> embed(text) -> store encrypted vector -> candidate retrieval (Annoy/Faiss) -> top-K -> reranker model call (small encoder + cross-attention) -> final scoring. For the spike we can test with 50k vectors and scale to your expected corpus.

Attached: sigma_dataflow_v1.png (high-level sequence diagram). I'll also add a short doc outlining RBAC roles and SSO flows to the Drive link.

Marissa
Head of Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Sigma Health — technical recap & observability asks

Great — thanks Laura / team. Finalizing runbook for the spike and owners below. Please review and confirm by EOD so we can lock the calendar.

Confirmed workshop: Tue Jun 23, 10:00–12:00 PT (Calendly link: https://calendly.com/rafael-mendes/redwood-sigma-tech-workshop)

Spike runbook (2 days)
- Day 0 (pre-work): Sigma infra creates staging VPC peering or whitelist, provides Okta client id/metadata (owner: Sigma Infra)
- Day 1 (workshop): integration code walk, tokens exchange demo, trace propagation demo, run a sample reranker against a 5k doc set (owners: Rafael, Connor, Sigma lead)
- Day 2 (validation): run performance test, collect latency headers and sample logs, iterate on batching and cache policies (owners: Marissa, Sigma SRE)

Action owners
- Provide staging creds & whitelist: Sigma Infra (infra@sigmahealth.com)
- Security checklist & PHI constraints: Laura (security lead cc'd by you)
- Data sample & expected RPS: Sigma data team
- Deliverables from Redwood: spike environment config, sample SDK snippets (node/java), example oauth-exchange flow, dashboard link with baseline metrics

Documents / links: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/sigma-health/tech-spike-notes (we'll drop the token-exchange spec there). HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/7890

If PHI requires Private deployment, pause hosted work and we'll swap in a Private deployment plan in the SOW. Otherwise we'll proceed with a staging environment in your account with encryption at rest.

Next: please confirm staging access and whether PHI is allowed to the hosted staging endpoint. Once confirmed we'll send the calendar invite and the spike checklist.

Thanks — Rafael
